- Native return (cold + warm): main.tsx:15 registerAuthDeepLinkHandler -> deepLinks.ts:186-208 (live listener installed BEFORE App.getLaunchUrl, serialized queue, per-(flowId,code) dedupe) -> exchangeCodeForSession -> Browser.close. iOS scene lifecycle: SceneDelegate.swift:7-33 forwards connectionOptions.urlContexts and openURLContexts into ApplicationDelegateProxy, which is what App.getLaunchUrl reads (@capacitor/app AppPlugin.swift:96-104, CAPApplicationDelegateProxy.swift:9-17). Android: AndroidManifest.xml:44-52 pins scheme+host+exact path, launchMode singleTask.
- Session restore / relaunch / logout / account switch: store.tsx:1153-1511 onAuthStateChange; signOut store.tsx:3776-3800 -> purgeLocalAccountData store.tsx:3731-3774.

WHAT IS CLEAN (verified, not assumed)
- PKCE-only and flow binding are NOT weakened: flowType:'pkce' and detectSessionInUrl:false are pinned (supabase.ts:88-94); BOTH callback paths refuse to exchange without a validated sb_flow_id (AuthCallbackPage.tsx:82-86, deepLinks.ts:123-128) and pass it explicitly, which makes auth-js do a slot-only verifier lookup (GoTrueClient.js:1592-1608). The old implicit-grant setSession fallback was deleted from the deep-link handler (git show 11910ec).
- No stale session survives logout: purgeLocalAccountData runs before the network call, and auth-js 2.111.0 `_signOut` calls removeCurrentSession() even when the server request errors, so SIGNED_OUT still fires offline. Verified in node_modules/@supabase/auth-js/dist/module/GoTrueClient.js `_signOut`.
- Account switch fails closed: identity change clears the E2EE runtime, bumps sessionGeneration, resets lifecycle/invite expiry, sets isAuthChecked(false) and replaces state with DEFAULT_STATE before any fetch (store.tsx:1163-1198), and every await is re-guarded on generation + session user id.
- Tokens are not persisted insecurely by app code: localStorage is a strict device-preference allowlist (store.tsx:240-252, 312-321); iOS excludes Library/WebKit|Cookies|HTTPStorages|kvstore from backup (AppDelegate.swift:51-74); Android allowBackup=false.

- Email/magic-link sign-in exists (supabase.ts:755-773) but NO UI calls it (grep: only types + tests), so it is not a shipping user path and is excluded per the dead-code rule.

findings.title: Every app foreground re-runs full account hydration; an offline foreground wipes loaded records and throws the user onto the full-screen sync-error page
findings.repro:
1. Sign in on the phone and open the app on a record-bearing screen (home/story).
2. Switch to another app (or lock the phone) for a few seconds. document.visibilityState goes 'hidden'.
3. Lose connectivity in that moment - subway, elevator, lift-off, or a captive-portal Wi-Fi that accepts the socket.
4. Return to 곰신로그.
5. visibilitychange -> auth-js _recoverAndRefresh -> SIGNED_IN -> store re-hydration -> fetch fails -> the whole app is replaced by the full-screen '계정 정보를 확인하지 못했어요 / 인터넷 연결을 확인한 뒤 다시 시도해 주세요' page, with records/events/trips/coupleHighlights cleared. The only controls are '다시 시도' (reload, which fails the same way while offline) and '로그아웃'.
Online variant of the same trigger: every single foreground silently issues getUser() + the ~9-query full state read + signed-URL requests + an E2EE runtime re-install, which is battery and data the user never asked for.
findings.impact: A normal app-switch - the most common interaction on a phone - can eject the user from the app onto a dead-end error screen and clear the content they were reading, even though nothing about their session or account changed. Offline reading of already-loaded records becomes impossible after any backgrounding. Online, every foreground costs a full account re-sync.
findings.minimal_fix: src/lib/store.tsx only. Do not let a repeat event for an already-hydrated identity tear down the loaded state. Smallest safe change: inside the `if (session?.user)` branch, when `hydratedUserIdRef.current === sessionUser.id` and `!identityChanged`, treat a failed hydration as non-fatal - skip `setAuthSyncUnavailable(true)` and skip the `records: []/events: []/trips: []/coupleHighlights: []` reset at 1365-1376, keeping the previously hydrated state (the existing offline banner already covers this case). Optionally also add `event === 'SIGNED_IN'` to the 1216 short-circuit; note src/lib/store.test.tsx:444-446 currently relies on a second same-user SIGNED_IN re-fetching couple state, so that test has to move to refreshCoupleLifecycle/realtime if the full short-circuit is taken.
findings.test_needed: In src/lib/store.test.tsx: hydrate user-a successfully, then emit a SECOND SIGNED_IN for user-a with fetchFullStateFromDB failing (offline classification) and assert (a) authSyncUnavailable stays false and (b) the previously loaded records are still present. Add a second case asserting a repeat same-user SIGNED_IN does not re-issue auth.getUser()/fetchFullStateFromDB when hydration already succeeded.

findings.title: Launch can sit on the unescapable splash spinner for minutes: nothing bounds the wait for the first auth event when session-restore's token refresh stalls
findings.evidence:
store.tsx:426 `const [isAuthChecked, setIsAuthChecked] = useState(!supabase);` - false whenever Supabase is configured. store.tsx:3988 `isReady: isHydrated && isAuthChecked`. App.tsx:326-332 renders ONLY a spinner while `!isReady`, ahead of every route including /auth/callback. The only writers of setIsAuthChecked(true) are inside the onAuthStateChange callback (store.tsx:1220, 1240, 1464, 1486, 1495) - there is no timer, watchdog or fallback anywhere (grep for setTimeout in store.tsx returns 1929/1963/2183/3121, none of them auth-gate related).

That first callback cannot fire until auth-js finishes initializing: GoTrueClient.js:3626-3637 `(async () => { await this.initializePromise; ... await this._emitInitialSession(id); })()`; initializePromise resolves only after `_initialize()` (:344-351), which at :419 does `await this._recoverAndRefresh()`; that awaits `_callRefreshToken` -> `_refreshAccessToken` (:3993-4018) whose `_request(this.fetch, 'POST', .../token?grant_type=refresh_token', ...)` carries NO AbortController and no deadline - the retry predicate only re-fires on an already-settled retryable error.

The app's own fetch deadline deliberately excludes this request: src/lib/oauthPkce.ts:21 `return url.pathname === '/auth/v1/token' && url.searchParams.get('grant_type') === 'pkce';` and :67 `if (!isPkceTokenRequest(input)) return fetchImpl(input, init);`. So the refresh grant is unwrapped, and the wall clock is left entirely to the platform socket timeout (60s+ per attempt on WKWebView, longer on a stalled Android WebView connection), multiplied by the backoff retries.
findings.repro:
1. Sign in, then leave the app unopened long enough for the access token to be within 90s of expiry (any overnight gap qualifies).
2. Join a network that accepts TCP connections but never answers - hotel/cafe/base captive-portal Wi-Fi is the everyday case; `pfctl`/Charles 'no response' reproduces it deterministically.
3. Cold-launch the app.
4. auth-js blocks in _recoverAndRefresh -> _refreshAccessToken; INITIAL_SESSION is never emitted; isAuthChecked stays false; App renders only the coral spinner. No message, no retry button, no way out but force-quit - which reproduces on the next launch.
findings.impact: On a stalled (not cleanly failed) network the app appears hung at launch for a minute or more, with no explanation and no escape, on the one screen that has no navigation. Reads as a crashed app to the user.
findings.minimal_fix: Two options, both one file. (a) src/lib/oauthPkce.ts: widen isPkceTokenRequest to bound any `/auth/v1/token` request (or add a second predicate for grant_type=refresh_token) so createPkceTimeoutFetch's AUTH_CALLBACK_TIMEOUT_MS applies to the refresh grant too. (b) src/lib/store.tsx: in the effect at 1153, start a `window.setTimeout(() => setIsAuthChecked(true), AUTH_SYNC_TIMEOUT_MS)` cleared by the first auth event, so the splash always releases and the existing authSyncUnavailable/onboarding routing decides what to show.
findings.test_needed: src/lib/store.test.tsx: render StoreProvider with an onAuthStateChange mock that never invokes its callback, advance fake timers past AUTH_SYNC_TIMEOUT_MS, and assert the Probe reports ready. Plus src/lib/oauthPkce.test.ts: assert a `/auth/v1/token?grant_type=refresh_token` request is aborted at AUTH_CALLBACK_TIMEOUT_MS if option (a) is taken.

findings.title: The logout escape hatch on the fail-closed screens awaits an unbounded network RPC before purging anything
findings.repro:
1. Reach the '계정 정보를 확인하지 못했어요' screen (P1 above, or a cold launch with a broken connection).
2. Tap 로그아웃 - the documented way off that screen.

findings.minimal_fix: src/lib/store.tsx:3791 - wrap the hygiene call in the existing helper: `await withTimeout(revokeOwnPushTokens(), <short ms>, { ok: false });` (withTimeout is already imported at store.tsx:211). The migration-048 handover DELETE is the real boundary, as the comment at 3785-3789 states, so a timed-out revoke is safe to skip.

findings.title: Sign-in screen shows no login buttons, no error and no retry if the GoTrue settings probe never settles
findings.evidence:
supabase.ts:60-76 fetchAuthProviderAvailability issues a bare `await fetch(`${SUPABASE_URL}/auth/v1/settings`, { headers: { apikey: SUPABASE_KEY }, cache: 'no-store' })` with no AbortController and no timeout; it is a direct global fetch, so createPkceTimeoutFetch does not apply.

OnboardingPage.tsx:135-147 only sets authProvidersResolved in `.then`/`.catch`, and every element of the landing screen's sign-in area is gated on it: :1069 `{authProvidersResolved && isIOS && authProviders.apple && (` (Apple), :1081 `{authProvidersResolved && authProviders.google && (` (Google), and :1096 `{authProvidersResolved && !authProviders.google && !(isIOS && authProviders.apple) && (` - the alert AND the '다시 시도' button at :1101-1107. A pending promise leaves all three unrendered.
findings.repro:
1. Fresh install (or signed-out state) on a network where requests stall rather than fail - captive portal, or a proxy holding the connection.
2. Open the app; the landing screen renders the age/terms checkboxes and the intro copy.
3. The /auth/v1/settings request never settles, so authProvidersResolved stays false: no Google button, no Apple button, no error text, no retry button. The user sees a sign-in screen with nothing to sign in with and no explanation.
findings.impact: First-run users on a stalled network are stranded on a login screen with no reachable login control and no way to retry short of killing the app - the worst possible moment for a silent dead end.
findings.minimal_fix: src/lib/supabase.ts:60-76 - give the probe a deadline (AbortController + AUTH_CALLBACK_TIMEOUT_MS, or wrap the call in the existing withTimeout from src/lib/async.ts with a `null` fallback) so it always settles and OnboardingPage falls into its existing resolved-with-no-provider branch, which already renders the alert and the 다시 시도 button.
findings.test_needed: src/lib/authProviderAvailability.test.ts: stub globalThis.fetch with a never-settling promise, advance fake timers, and assert fetchAuthProviderAvailability resolves to null. Plus an OnboardingPage test asserting the '다시 시도' retry button is rendered when the availability probe stalls.

findings.title: A dropped realtime channel wipes the staged-post retry pointer, stranding a private caption row and forcing a duplicate post
findings.evidence:
When a profile post's photos fail to upload, the caption row is already on the server as a private record and the only pointer back to it is persisted locally (SharedProfile.tsx:306-316 `setPostRetryRecordId(result.recordId); storePostRetry(userId, { recordId, coupleId, desiredPrivate })`). The restore effect deletes that pointer whenever the record is not in `state.records`:
```
132    const retryRecord = state.records.find((record) => (
133      record.id === stored.recordId
…
138    if (!retryRecord) {
139      clearStoredPostRetry(userId);
140      return;
141    }
```
Guarded only by `if (!isReady || !userId || !coupleId || postRetryRecordId) return;` (SharedProfile.tsx:125) — it never consults `sharedSyncStatus`.

`state.records` is emptied while `profile.couple.coupleId` is kept by quarantineSharedAccess (store.tsx:1561-1592):
```
1566    setSharedSyncStatus('unavailable');
1567    const nextState: AppState = {
1568      ...current,
…
1577      records: [],
```
Its triggers are exactly the flaky-network conditions that cause the upload failure in the first place: a records fetch that fails (store.tsx:1822-1824) and a realtime channel `CHANNEL_ERROR | TIMED_OUT | CLOSED` (store.tsx:2045-2055).

The codebase already knows this window is not evidence of absence — RecordPage.tsx:575 guards the identical "record not found" judgement with `if (sharedSyncStatus === 'unavailable') return;` and RecordPage.tsx:563-570 explains why. SharedProfile has no equivalent.
findings.repro:
1. 우리 → `+` → pick photos → 공유 on a weak connection so the uploads fail. Toast: "사진은 아직 붙이지 못했고 글은 나만 보기로 보관했어요…"; the header button becomes "게시물 사진 이어서 올리기".
2. The same weak connection drops the realtime socket (or one records refresh fails) → quarantineSharedAccess sets `records: []`.
3. Navigate to 홈 and back to 우리 (or relaunch the app) so SharedProfile remounts with `postRetryRecordId === null`.
4. The effect runs with `state.records === []`, does not find the row, and calls `clearStoredPostRetry`.
5. Connectivity returns and records reload. The button is back to "게시물 만들기"; the staged row is gone from the composer's reach.
findings.impact: The user's caption is stranded on the server as a private, non-profile-post record they never asked for and cannot reach from the profile screen. The 'attach the photos to the same row' recovery that SharedProfile.tsx:228-261 was built for is unreachable, so retrying creates a second record with the same caption — one visible post plus one invisible private duplicate per failed attempt.
findings.minimal_fix: In the restore effect at src/features/us/SharedProfile.tsx:122-145, take `sharedSyncStatus` from `useStore()` and return early while it is `'unavailable'` (and while `state.records.length === 0`), so only an authoritative record set may clear the pointer — mirroring RecordPage.tsx:575.

findings.title: A record whose photos all fail to upload is appended to a record list a realtime refresh already replaced, so it renders twice
findings.evidence:
The final commit appends unconditionally, with no check for an entry already carrying this id:
```
2792    const recordToCommit = finalRecord;
2793    updateStateImmediately((current) =>
2794      isCurrentLinkedCouple(workspace) && stateMatchesLinkedCouple(current, workspace)
2795        ? { ...current, records: [...current.records, recordToCommit] }
2796        : current,
2797    );
```
Meanwhile the client's own INSERT is broadcast back to it and schedules a wholesale replacement of the same array:
```
2016      { event: '*', schema: 'public', table: 'daily_records', filter: `couple_id=eq.${coupleId}` },
2017      () => scheduleRefresh('records'),
```
debounced by `const REALTIME_DEBOUNCE_MS = 250;` (store.tsx:180) into `refreshSlice('records')`, which does `updateStateImmediately((current) => isCurrentRefresh() ? { ...current, records } : current)` (store.tsx:1849-1853).

Normally the attachment patch (store.tsx:2736) fires a second realtime event whose refresh overwrites the duplicate. Rejections carry only `{index, reason}` — no text, ids, paths.

Real recordIds and exact dates stay in JS-only `sources`/`days` maps and never enter the payload. Attachment names/URLs/paths are dropped by `projectBriefingMediaKinds` (`normalize.ts:213-234`).
- The wire payload to native is narrower still: `pipeline.ts:614-617` sends only `{requestId, items:[{itemOrdinal, candidates:[{candidateOrdinal, text}]}]}`. No dayOrdinal, period, mediaKinds, ids, or dates cross.
- The mechanical no-model-authored-text boundary holds independently of the verifier: `pipeline.ts:655-665` builds every displayed part from `seg.candidates[choice.candidateOrdinal].text` (a TypeScript-owned exact substring) plus a fixed template in `fallback.ts:110-118`. Even if a provider returned a `text` field, nothing reads it. `verify.ts:489-513` additionally bounds `candidateOrdinal` against `requestedItems[itemOrd].candidates.length`, so the array index cannot be out of range.
- Group-to-record binding cannot be mis-attributed: `pipeline.ts:716-722` re-validates `isExactContiguousMatch` against the actual period event sequence before rendering a merged item, and falls back to per-event deterministic text otherwise.
- Zero logging and zero persistence confirmed by grep: no `console.*` anywhere under `src/lib/partnerBriefing/`, `src/components/widgets/PartnerBriefingCard.tsx`, or `src/features/story/`. All briefing state is React state/refs.

## 2. Native on-device providers — no server inference, no logs
- Android `packages/capacitor-on-device-briefing/android/.../OnDeviceBriefingEngine.kt:228-256`: ML Kit GenAI Prompt (`Generation.getClient()`, on-device via AICore), fresh model per inference, `close()` in `finally`, no network, no `Log.*`/`println` anywhere in the module (grep returned only the comment claiming so).
- iOS `packages/capacitor-on-device-briefing/ios/.../OnDeviceBriefing.swift:150-160`: `SystemLanguageModel.default` + per-request `LanguageModelSession` (on-device Foundation Models). No `print`/`NSLog`/`os_log` in either plugin package. Error mapping switches on typed error codes, never on raw messages.
- Both bridges reject unknown keys and cap size; on any failure the pipeline degrades to deterministic text rather than retrying elsewhere. On web/PWA `nativeOnDeviceBriefing.ts:44-51` returns `unsupported` so no content leaves JS at all.

## 3. Plaintext at rest and in transit
- `localStorage` is a hard allowlist: `src/lib/store.tsx:248` persists only `carryOverDevicePrefs(state)` derived from `DEVICE_PREF_CARRY_OVER_KEYS` (`store.tsx:312-321` — hasSeenInstallPrompt, locale, soldierWidgetLayout, theme, widgetLayout). No records, profile, couple, or auth.
- Composer drafts (the most sensitive unsent text) are memory-only and keyed by userId (`src/lib/composerDraft.ts:27`), cleared by `purgeLocalAccountData` (`store.tsx:3742`). Avatar photos live under their own keys and are explicitly wiped by `clearAllAvatars()` (`store.tsx:3759`).
- E2EE local state stores AES-GCM ciphertext only, key held by Keychain/Keystore (`src/app/e2ee/protectedLocalState.ts:99-135`); key loss is a terminal error rather than a create-a-fresh-key downgrade.
- Device keys never leave the secure element: `packages/capacitor-device-keys/ios/.../DeviceKeys.swift` and `LocalKeys.kt` expose sign/derive/seal/open by handle only; `load()` fails closed on an unknown handle.
- Service worker (`public/sw.js:52-93`) refuses navigations and anything but same-origin script/style/image/font/manifest, so no Supabase API or media response is ever written to Cache Storage.
- Only one non-Supabase `fetch` exists in `src/` (`src/lib/supabase.ts:63`, the auth settings probe). CSP in `public/_headers:21` is `default-src 'self'` with connect-src pinned to the validated Supabase origin. OCR is genuinely local (`src/lib/placeOcr.ts:78-84`, `workerBlobURL: false`, local worker/core/lang paths).
- Analytics cannot carry content by construction: `src/lib/productEvents.ts:80-92` has no free-text field, and `FORBIDDEN_EVENT_SUBSTRINGS` bans cycle/health/emotion/dwell kinds. Push notifications use one constant sentence with no record id (`supabase/functions/send-push/handler.ts:47-56`); local notifications use `genericCopy` (`src/lib/notifications.ts:103-106`). Edge-function `logEvent` calls pass counts/outcomes only.
- Data export (`src/lib/dataExport.ts:9-11`) filters strictly on `record.userId === userId`, never `authorRole`.

## 4. Record protection / plaintext downgrade
`src/app/records/contentCrypto.ts:122-152` derives the domain from the record's own visibility, honours both the server write floor and the local couple barrier, and returns `{mode:'refused'}` rather than plaintext when no ACTIVE epoch or key is available. The single reachable writer, `src/lib/records.ts:481-487`, fails closed on that refusal and never falls through; when it does encrypt, `records.ts:499-511` blanks `log_text`/`reaction`/`attachments`/`emotion_flow`/`record_time` in the same statement. `VITE_E2EE_DEVICE_PROTECTION_ENABLED` is documented as `false` for release (`docs/APP_STORE_RELEASE_PLAN_2026-08-25.md:108`), and every protection UI/barrier is gated on `isDeviceProtectionEnabled()` consistently (SettingsPage:144/215, store.tsx:674/780), so there is no screen offering protection that silently does nothing.

## 5. Private / author-only enforcement
`src/lib/privacy.ts` is applied at ingest in all three record writers (`sync.ts:420`, `store.tsx:1718`, `store.tsx:1828`), each passing a non-empty authenticated `userId`, so the role fallback in `isOwnRecord` is never the deciding branch. `partnerDay.ts:356` re-applies `visibleRecordsForViewer` before building the surface, so the briefing corpus receives already-sanitised records. Server side, the partner SELECT policy pins `is_private = false` (`supabase/migrations/005_secure_rls_policies.sql:66-72`) and the storage SELECT policy repeats it per object (`supabase/migrations/028_restore_couple_media_authorization.sql:59-81`).

## 6. Native shell hardening
`capacitor.config.ts:36-52` sets `webContentsDebuggingEnabled: false` on both platforms; `android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:11-17` sets `allowBackup="false"`, `dataExtractionRules`, and `usesCleartextTraffic="false"`, with a minimal permission set.

## Noted but deliberately NOT reported as findings
- Signed media URLs have a 1-hour TTL (`src/lib/records.ts:SIGNED_URL_TTL_SECONDS`). Supabase evaluates RLS at signing time, so a URL issued while a record was shared stays fetchable for up to an hour after the author flips it private. This is inherent to signed URLs, not a code defect; the record itself disappears from the partner's client on the next sync and the URL is never persisted (state is not written to localStorage).
- iOS declares `promptOverheadUtf8Bytes = 256` while the session `instructions` string is ~280 bytes and is not counted by `prompt()` (Android has a compile-time `check()` for the same budget; iOS has none). Worst case is `exceededContextWindowSize` -> `malformedOutput` -> deterministic fallback for that batch. Quality degradation, not a privacy or availability defect.

## Not verified (out of reach here)
Real-device behaviour of the iOS Foundation Models and Android ML Kit paths (Gate C/D/E remain UNVERIFIED per the architecture doc); whether the remote Supabase project actually has migrations 005/028 applied (the repo ledger is not proof of deployment); and the runtime value of `VITE_PARTNER_BRIEFING_ENABLED` in the release build, which I could not read (env files are off-limits) — I audited the flag-on path on the assumption it may ship enabled.

Method: read the amended contract (docs/PARTNER_BRIEFING_ARCHITECTURE.md, including its uncommitted diff) and every module in src/lib/partnerBriefing/*, plus the active call path PaperHome -> /story/partner -> StoryRoute -> StoryViewer -> PartnerBriefingCard, usePartnerDay, records.ts mapRow, and both native plugins (OnDeviceBriefing.swift / OnDeviceBriefingPlugin.swift / OnDeviceBriefingEngine.kt / OnDeviceBriefingPlugin.kt). I did not run the repo's vitest suite (read-only); instead I transpiled the real, unmodified modules with the repo's own esbuild into /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/out and executed them in node, so every claim below comes from running the actual shipped code.

CLEAN (verified, not just read):
- Compression, not selection. Randomized property run over 216 configurations (n = 1/2/5/30/100/300 records, three provider envelopes including a deliberately tiny one, and four provider scenarios: all-ok, every-2nd-batch-fails, wrong-correlation, malformed-with-extra-key) found 0 coverage violations: every eligible record appears exactly once across days/sections/items, no duplicates, overview.sourceRecordIds is the exact union, and sourceCount always equals the input count. Multi-day is retained; days sort ascending by dayOrdinal.
- Fail-closed corpus. corpus.ts:135-170 rejects non-active couples, unresolved/equal identities, unpersisted rows, wrong-partner rows, isPrivate !== false, and contentUnavailable. Rejection metadata is only {index, reason}; I confirmed no log text, URL, or id is carried out.
- No structured cycle/bleeding/pain/symptom/health field can reach the payload: DailyRecord (src/types/index.ts:124-161) carries no such field, and normalize.ts:301-307 projects a closed allowlist {ordinal, dayOrdinal, period, text, mediaKinds}. emotionFlow/emotionAnalysis (author-only) are likewise not projected.
- No real recordId/userId/coupleId/date/time/URL/path/key crosses the native boundary. nativeOnDeviceBriefing.ts:174-178 sends only {requestId, locale, items}; items carry only itemOrdinal + {candidateOrdinal, text}. Both native parsers enforce exact key sets (Swift:123,136; Kotlin:213,237) and reject anything else. recordId binding happens only in TypeScript (pipeline.ts:665, 682, 740, 761) via sourceMap.
- Verifier is a genuinely closed schema (verify.ts:113-117 allowlists, 357 version===2, 394 groupOrdinal===index, 419 group size 2..4, 468 strict request order, 504 candidate membership, 531 full coverage). A provider response carrying text/claim/label is rejected; I confirmed the malformed-with-extra-key scenario falls back deterministically without contaminating sibling batches.
- Long records are never split across provider requests: chunk.ts prepareEvent returns >1 segment, and pipeline.ts:497-508 forces that ordinal to a deterministic singleton, so fragments never reach the model. A single unfittable cluster returns null and also becomes deterministic (verified: no truncated text can reach a candidate).
- Timeout/cancellation/stale rejection is sound: one whole-run deadline recomputed before each await (pipeline.ts:450-453, 598), cancel() notified on timeout and abort (pipeline.ts:277-281, 336-338), PartnerBriefingRunner aborts the prior run and drops late results (pipeline.ts:833), and usePartnerBriefing gates commits on inputKey identity plus an isMounted flag (usePartnerBriefing.ts:233-240, 269).
- Viewing a briefing never writes CONFIRMED. usePartnerDay's persist effect can only write OUTSTANDING/KNOWN (usePartnerDay.ts:139-147); acknowledge() is the sole CONFIRMED writer and is reachable only from ClosingCard's onAcknowledge (StoryRoute.tsx:226-231, 270). Exact-original navigation is preserved per part (PartnerBriefingCard.tsx:204 -> StoryRoute.tsx:187-195).
- No logging or persistence anywhere in src/lib/partnerBriefing/* or PartnerBriefingCard.tsx (grep for console/localStorage/sessionStorage/indexedDB/fetch returns only a doc comment).
- Progressive disclosure adds 20 groups per press and always reaches every item.

NOT reported (checked and judged below the bar): the "N개 더 보기" label counts hidden source records while the press reveals 20 groups, so on a large window it overstates what one press shows (PartnerBriefingCard.tsx:88 vs :237); formatDeterministicBriefingItemText re-segments without passing locale (fallback.ts:159); Android does not pre-emptively cancel a prior in-flight request the way iOS does, but the pipeline is sequential and JS cancels on timeout. I also benchmarked the synchronous baseline generation (Intl.Segmenter over the whole corpus during render): 2ms for 120 records, so it is not a bottleneck.

findings.title: The 'night' period wraps midnight, so early-morning and late-night records merge into one group and the night section renders above the morning section
findings.evidence:
normalize.ts:132-134 maps BOTH 00:00-04:59 and 22:00-23:59 to 'night':
    if ((hour >= 0 && hour <= 4) || (hour >= 22 && hour <= 23)) { return 'night'; }
pipeline.ts:513 then buckets by day+period only:
    const key = String(evt.dayOrdinal) + '_' + String(evt.period);
so both night bands land in one contiguousRun (pipeline.ts:576-580) and can be grouped together, and pipeline.ts:717 renders sections in Map insertion order:
    for (const [period, periodEvents] of dayGroup.entries()) {
which is first-appearance order, putting 'night' first for any day containing a 00:00-04:59 record. fallback.ts:525 has the identical ordering, so the deterministic baseline every user sees first has it too.

Executed against the real transpiled modules (records at 02:10, 09:00, 14:00, 19:00, 23:40 on one day, FakeBriefingProvider):
  events -> period : 0:night 1:morning 2:afternoon 3:evening 4:night
  deterministic section order: night[r0,r4] -> morning[r1] -> afternoon[r2] -> evening[r3]
  refined (generation: on_device), 밤 section:
    item parts -> r0: “새벽에 잠이 안 왔어요.”라고 기록했어요.  ||  r4: “자기 전에 네 생각했어요.”라고 기록했어요.
Ordinals 0 and 4 are one item despite ordinals 1, 2 and 3 lying between them. Over 40 randomized single-day runs, 17 of 268 multi-part items had non-contiguous parts; the worst joined ordinals 1 and 25 (24 records in between) under the 밤 heading.

The contract requires "contiguous source items grouped into 2-4 items per group" and "groups never cross day or period boundaries, or a fallback/media-only original gap" (docs/PARTNER_BRIEFING_ARCHITECTURE.md, Provenance and v2 grouping contract), and the native instructions say the same (OnDeviceBriefing.swift:54 "Group contiguous items").

findings.title: maxInputTextGraphemes means 'per record' in TypeScript but 'per whole request' in both native parsers, so batches the pipeline proves valid are rejected and silently fall back to deterministic
findings.evidence:
Batching proves only the UTF-8 byte budget — there is no grapheme term anywhere in it. pipeline.ts:379:
    if (canItemsFitInEnvelope(testItems, envelope, FIXED_PLACEHOLDER_REQUEST_ID)) {
and canItemsFitInEnvelope (pipeline.ts:148-197) checks only request bytes and response-reserve bytes. In TypeScript the grapheme cap is applied per single record (chunk.ts:237-240, `clusters.length <= envelope.maxInputTextGraphemes` for one event) and the per-chunk accumulation at chunk.ts:376-384 belongs to chunkPartnerBriefingEvents, whose modelChunks the pipeline uses only to detect split records (pipeline.ts:497-508) and never to size a request.

Both native parsers instead accumulate across every candidate of every item in the request and reject the whole call:
  OnDeviceBriefingPlugin.swift:143-146
    totalGraphemes += text.count
    guard totalGraphemes <= OnDeviceBriefing.maxInputTextGraphemes else { return nil }
  OnDeviceBriefingPlugin.kt:259-263
    totalGraphemes += graphemes
    if (totalGraphemes > OnDeviceBriefing.MAX_INPUT_TEXT_GRAPHEMES) { return null }
returning nil/null -> reject(.badRequest) -> E_BAD_REQUEST -> nativeOnDeviceBriefing.ts:91-92 maps it to 'malformed' -> verify.ts rejects -> pipeline.ts:637-639 marks the batch failed.

Executed with the exact iOS constants (OnDeviceBriefing.swift:45-48: 4096/256/512/1000) against the real batchCandidateSegments and buildBriefingExtractCandidates:
  ko 340 graphemes/record x3: items=3 bytes=2783/3328 TSfits=true nativeGraphemes=1023/1000 -> NATIVE REJECTS
  ko 520 graphemes/record x2: items=2 bytes=2764/3328 TSfits=true nativeGraphemes=1042/1000 -> NATIVE REJECTS
  en 601 graphemes/record x3: items=3 bytes=2063/3328 TSfits=true nativeGraphemes=1803/1000 -> NATIVE REJECTS
The same holds for Android (4096/512/1024/1000, OnDeviceBriefingEngine.kt:70-73).
findings.repro:
1. Build with VITE_PARTNER_BRIEFING_ENABLED=true on a device where availability() returns 'ready' (iOS 26 with Apple Intelligence, or an ML Kit-capable Android).
2. Have the partner write three fairly long diary entries (~340 Korean characters each — roughly a full screen of text) within the same period of one day, e.g. 09:10, 09:40 and 10:20.
3. Open /story/partner and expand the briefing.
4. Observed: briefing.generation is 'deterministic' (or 'hybrid' when other buckets succeed) and that period's records render as ungrouped one-per-record bullets. The native layer rejected the request with E_BAD_REQUEST before the model ever ran; nothing is surfaced to the user or to the caller.
5. Shorten one entry so the batch's candidate graphemes total under 1000 and the same three records group normally.
findings.impact: On-device grouping silently stops happening for exactly the users who need compression most — the ones whose partner writes long entries during a missed window. The output stays correct and every record is still shown (deterministic fallback is sound), so this is quality degradation rather than data loss, but it is invisible: no error, no telemetry, and the 'on_device' vs 'deterministic' classification is the only trace. It also means Gate C/D device verification can report 'deterministic' and look like a model-availability problem rather than a contract mismatch.
findings.minimal_fix: Make the TypeScript batcher enforce the same meaning the native parsers use. In src/lib/partnerBriefing/pipeline.ts, extend canItemsFitInEnvelope (lines 148-197) to also sum grapheme counts over every candidate of every item (reuse countGraphemes from ./chunk) and return false when that total exceeds envelope.maxInputTextGraphemes; batchCandidateSegments at line 379/399 then splits batches correctly with no other change. dimension: iOS native on-device AI (GATE 4) — Foundation Models plugin, availability gating, concurrency, malformed-output rejection, payload allowlist
notes:
SCOPE / CALL PATH TRACED
StoryRoute.tsx:62 (`mode === 'today' && import.meta.env.VITE_PARTNER_BRIEFING_ENABLED === 'true'`) -> StoryRoute.tsx:126 passes `nativeOnDeviceBriefingProvider` -> usePartnerBriefing.ts:223 `runner.run` -> pipeline.ts:420 `runPartnerBriefingPipeline` -> pipeline.ts:620 `executeProviderSelectExtractsWithTimeout` -> nativeOnDeviceBriefing.ts:174 `port.selectExtracts` -> OnDeviceBriefingPlugin.swift:41 -> OnDeviceBriefingEngine.select -> OnDeviceBriefing.selectWithSystemModel -> `LanguageModelSession.respond(generating: GeneratedBriefingPlan.self)`. Note the flag is not set in `.env.example`, CI, or any build script I could read (I did not open `.env`), so on a default release build this whole path is dark; findings below are scoped to the flag being on for GATE 4.

WHAT I VERIFIED AS CLEAN (with evidence, not assumption)

1. iOS 15 floor vs iOS 26 requirement — SAFE, verified empirically, not by reading.
   `xcrun --sdk iphoneos swiftc -typecheck -swift-version 5 -target arm64-apple-ios15.0` on OnDeviceBriefing.swift compiles with zero diagnostics against iPhoneOS26.5.sdk (Xcode 26.6). Compiling to an object and running `nm -mu` shows EVERY FoundationModels symbol as `(undefined) weak external` (e.g. `_$s16FoundationModels16GenerationSchemaV...`), so ld will emit LC_LOAD_WEAK_DYLIB and the app will not fail dyld on iOS 15–25. Podspec `s.ios.deployment_target = '15.0'` / `s.swift_version = '5.9'` are consistent with the shipped capacitor-on-device-summary plugin that already uses the same `#if canImport(FoundationModels)` + `@available(iOS 26.0, *)` pattern.

2. Every FoundationModels API the plugin uses exists in the shipping SDK — checked against `.../FoundationModels.framework/.../arm64e-apple-ios.swiftinterface`: `SystemLanguageModel.default` (:573), `Availability.available/.unavailable(.deviceNotEligible/.appleIntelligenceNotEnabled/.modelNotReady)` (:558-569), `supportsLocale(_:)` (:589), `LanguageModelSession(model:tools:@InstructionsBuilder instructions:)` (:339), `respond(to:generating:options:)` (:381), `GenerationOptions(sampling:temperature:maximumResponseTokens:)` (:1324), `SamplingMode.greedy` (:1314), `Response.content` (:347), and all nine `GenerationError` cases the switch enumerates (:424-432). Bare `case .rateLimited:` patterns match cases carrying associated `Context` values, so the exhaustive switch is valid.

3. Availability degradation is graceful end to end. iOS < 26 or no FoundationModels -> `.unsupported`; `.modelNotReady` -> `preparing`; deviceNotEligible/appleIntelligenceNotEnabled -> `model_unavailable`; unknown locale -> `locale_unsupported`. nativeOnDeviceBriefing.ts:129-136 clamps to the 5-value allowlist and returns `model_unavailable` on any throw; pipeline.ts:467 short-circuits to `generateDeterministicPartnerBriefing` for anything but `ready`. No blank screen, no crash — usePartnerBriefing.ts:123 has already rendered a synchronous deterministic baseline before the provider is ever consulted.

4. Korean locale — `localeIdentifier(for:)` maps 'ko' -> "ko_KR" and gates on `model.supportsLocale(Locale(identifier:))` (OnDeviceBriefing.swift:74) before every run, plus `GenerationError.unsupportedLanguageOrLocale` -> `locale_unsupported` at :198. `briefingLocale` in StoryRoute.tsx:61 is 'ko' unless `state.locale === 'en'`. Correct.

5. Cancel-before-registration — genuinely handled and I confirmed there is no suspension point between the `cancelledBeforeStart` check (OnDeviceBriefing.swift:251) and `inFlight = (requestId, task)` (:272), so the actor executes that prefix atomically; a cancel can only interleave at `await task.value`, where it hits the in-flight branch. The list is capped at 32 (`maximumPendingCancellations`, :221/:238-242) so it cannot grow unbounded, and requestIds are `crypto.randomUUID()` (pipeline.ts:82-95), so a stale pending-cancel entry can never poison a later request. The `defer` at :273 compares requestId before clearing, so a superseded run cannot clobber a newer one's slot.

6. Cancellation during inference / timeout-then-late-response — `await task.value` releases the actor, so `cancel` runs while inference is in flight. On the JS side pipeline.ts:327 `Promise.race([callPromise, timeoutPromise, abortPromise])` plus the `settled` latch in nativeOnDeviceBriefing.ts:160-166 means a late native resolve is dropped, and both listeners are removed on every exit path. `safeCancel` fires from the timer and again in `finally` when `didTimeout`; the `cancelledBeforeStart.contains` guard dedupes it.

7. Payload allowlist / no id-url-path leakage — verified end to end, this is the strongest part of the change. `requireExactKeys` (OnDeviceBriefingPlugin.swift:172) rejects any unexpected top-level key on all four methods; `parseItems` requires `Set(entry.keys) == Set(["itemOrdinal","candidates"])` and `Set(candidate.keys) == Set(["candidateOrdinal","text"])` with ordinals forced to equal their index (:123-138); `exactInteger` rejects Bool, negatives and non-integral doubles (:177-183). The prompt is only `"Items JSON:\n" + itemsJSON` (OnDeviceBriefing.swift:91) over that allowlisted shape. Upstream, normalize.ts:298-299 derives `text` solely from `record.log` and media from kinds only — no recordId, userId, coupleId, date, attachment URL or path can reach the model. The `@Generable` structs contain only `Int` fields, so the model has no channel to emit displayable text.

8. Capacitor plumbing — `call.resolve` from the `Task` is safe (`CapacitorBridge.toJs` at :583 hops to `DispatchQueue.main`); plugin methods run on the serial background `"bridge"` queue (:130), not main, so inference never blocks the UI thread; `code` survives to JS (`CAPPluginCallError.code`, PluginCallResult.swift:81 -> native-bridge.js:947 copies error keys onto a `cap.Exception`), so `nativeErrorCode` in the adapter really does read E_BUSY/E_QUOTA/E_CANCELLED/E_BAD_REQUEST/E_MALFORMED.

9. Byte-envelope direction is safe: TS `canItemsFitInEnvelope` serializes `{requestId, items}` (~55 bytes larger than the Swift side's bare items array), so anything TS accepts also clears the Swift `data.count + overhead + reserve <= maxContext` check. No false E_BAD_REQUEST from size.

10. Existing tests are green (81 passing across nativeOnDeviceBriefing / verify / onDeviceBriefingBridge) — the three findings below all survive that suite, which is why they are worth reporting.

findings.title: promptOverheadUtf8Bytes still declares 256 while the rewritten grouping instructions now cost 295 UTF-8 bytes
findings.evidence:
The uncommitted diff roughly doubles the instruction string (OnDeviceBriefing.swift:53-55):

-    Choose one supplied candidate for every item. Return only itemOrdinal and candidateOrdinal. Keep every item once and in order. Never write text.
+    Group contiguous items into groups of 2–4; use a singleton only when the request contains exactly one item. Choose one supplied candidate for every item. Return only groupOrdinal, itemOrdinal, and candidateOrdinal. Keep every item once and in order across groups. Never write text.

but line 46 is unchanged: `static let promptOverheadUtf8Bytes = 256`.

Measured from the file: instructions = 281 chars / 283 UTF-8 bytes (the en-dash in '2–4' is 3 bytes), plus the `"Items JSON:\n"` prefix built at OnDeviceBriefing.swift:91 = 12 bytes. Actual overhead = 295 bytes vs 256 declared, a 39-byte shortfall.

That constant is the shared budget on both sides: Swift `parseItems` (OnDeviceBriefingPlugin.swift:163-165) and TS `canItemsFitInEnvelope` (pipeline.ts:437-441) both compute `maxContextUtf8Bytes - promptOverheadUtf8Bytes - responseReserveUtf8Bytes` from it, and it is published to JS verbatim via `capability()` (OnDeviceBriefingPlugin.swift:34).

The guard test cannot catch this: onDeviceBriefingBridge.test.ts:62 only asserts the source string `static let promptOverheadUtf8Bytes = 256` is present, so it stays green precisely because the constant was left stale.
findings.repro: Read the instruction literal at OnDeviceBriefing.swift:53-55 and byte-count it (283 bytes), add the 12-byte 'Items JSON:\n' prefix from :91, and compare to the 256 declared at :46. Any batch packed to the 3328-byte ceiling then sends 4135 bytes of prompt where the envelope arithmetic promised at most 4096.
findings.impact: The envelope stops being a proof. Requests can exceed their own declared context budget by ~39 bytes, so the 'proven to fit' guarantee the architecture doc claims no longer holds, and a future tightening of maxContextUtf8Bytes toward the real 4096-token window would start producing GenerationError.exceededContextWindowSize -> E_MALFORMED at the ceiling. Today the byte figure is a conservative proxy for a token window (3328 bytes of Korean is only ~700-1100 tokens), so no user is currently broken — this is invariant drift introduced by the diff, not a live break.
findings.minimal_fix: Raise `promptOverheadUtf8Bytes` to a value that actually covers the instructions plus prefix (e.g. 384) in packages/capacitor-on-device-briefing/ios/Sources/OnDeviceBriefingPlugin/OnDeviceBriefing.swift:46, mirror it in the Android engine constant, and update the pinned pair in src/lib/partnerBriefing/onDeviceBriefingBridge.test.ts:62 and onDeviceBriefingAndroidBridge.test.ts.
findings.test_needed: Replace the literal-string assertion in onDeviceBriefingBridge.test.ts with a computed one: extract the `instructions` heredoc and the prompt prefix from the Swift source, `Buffer.byteLength(..., 'utf8')` them, and assert the sum is <= the parsed `promptOverheadUtf8Bytes`. That test fails today (295 > 256) and cannot rot the next time the prompt is reworded.

findings.title: N+1: one uncached Supabase scope_keys query per encrypted record on every records refresh
findings.repro:
1. Sign in as a member of a connected couple whose device has completed E2EE bootstrap.
2. Let the couple accumulate records (each shared record is written GLE1 per contentCrypto.ts:136-141).
3. Background the app, then foreground it. `document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', handleVisibility)` at src/lib/store.tsx:2069 fires → src/lib/store.tsx:2063 `void reconcileOwnMembership()` → `reconcileSharedAccess` → src/lib/store.tsx:1702 `fetchRecordsResultFromDB(workspace.coupleId)`.
4. Watch the network panel: one GET to `daily_records`, then one GET to `scope_keys?domain=eq.couple&scope_id=eq.<coupleId>` PER ENCRYPTED RECORD, all fired at once by the `Promise.all`.
5. Same fan-out on the other hot path: tap the 'talk about' bookmark on any record (or have the partner post). The `daily_records` postgres_changes handler at src/lib/store.tsx:2016-2017 calls `scheduleRefresh('records')` → src/lib/store.tsx:1820 `fetchRecordsResultFromDB(coupleId)` → the same N queries.
findings.impact: Every return to the app and every record change fires one HTTP request per encrypted record against PostgREST. A couple 6 months into a service term with ~400 shared records issues ~400 concurrent identical `scope_keys` queries on each foreground. Because supabase-js runs over HTTP/2 there is no browser connection cap to throttle it, so the burst hits the Supabase connection pooler and rate limiter directly. Users see the home/story screen stall behind a spinner on every foreground, requests start failing under pooler pressure, and a failed records fetch is not benign — src/lib/store.tsx:1708-1712 treats it as `quarantineSharedAccess(workspace)`, which HIDES the couple's shared content. So the load spike degrades into shared data disappearing from the screen. Cost scales linearly with relationship length, i.e. it gets worse for exactly the most-retained users.

Invalidate that key wherever this module creates/activates/abandons an epoch so a rotation is still observed. If cache staleness is judged too risky for the write path, the alternative one-file fix is in `src/lib/records.ts`: resolve the (at most two) epoch lists ONCE before the `Promise.all` at line 266 and thread them into `mapRow`/`decryptRecordRow` as a per-fetch memo, leaving the write path untouched. findings.title: Batcher ignores the maxInputTextGraphemes limit the Android plugin advertises, so whole batches are hard-rejected as E_BAD_REQUEST
findings.evidence:
The Android plugin advertises a grapheme ceiling in its capability envelope and then enforces it as a TOTAL across every candidate in the request:

  Plugin.kt:71   put("maxInputTextGraphemes", OnDeviceBriefing.MAX_INPUT_TEXT_GRAPHEMES)   // 1000, Engine.kt:73
  Plugin.kt:259-263
      val graphemes = engine.countGraphemes(text)
      totalGraphemes += graphemes
      if (totalGraphemes > OnDeviceBriefing.MAX_INPUT_TEXT_GRAPHEMES) {
          return null
      }
  Plugin.kt:106-110   parseItems(...) == null -> reject(call, BriefingErrorCode.BAD_REQUEST)

The JS batcher that decides how many items go into one request never consults that field. batchCandidateSegments' only admission test is:

  pipeline.ts:379   if (canItemsFitInEnvelope(testItems, envelope, FIXED_PLACEHOLDER_REQUEST_ID)) {

and canItemsFitInEnvelope (pipeline.ts:148-196) reads only maxContextUtf8Bytes, promptOverheadUtf8Bytes and responseReserveUtf8Bytes — I grepped maxInputTextGraphemes across src/lib/partnerBriefing and it appears solely in chunk.ts (91, 238, 258, 380) and provider.ts:157, never in pipeline.ts. The chunk.ts bound does not cover this: step 4 (pipeline.ts:489-508) uses chunkPartnerBriefingEvents only to derive forcedFallbackOrdinals and to detect split events, and step 6 (pipeline.ts:559-581) then rebuilds batches from the raw `events` list, not from modelChunks.

The byte budget alone is 4096-512-1024 = 2560 bytes for the request JSON. Korean text is 3 UTF-8 bytes per grapheme, so Korean records cap out near 830 graphemes and never trip the native limit — which is exactly why this is invisible in the Korean-only tests. Latin text is 1 byte per grapheme, so a batch can legally carry well over 2000 graphemes by bytes while blowing straight past the 1000-grapheme native cap. Long single records are not a rescue: prepareEvent (chunk.ts:228-270) only forces a fallback for one oversized event, never for the sum of several small ones.

On rejection, nativeOnDeviceBriefing.ts:91-92 maps E_BAD_REQUEST to 'malformed', pipeline.ts:630-639 marks the batch failed, and every item in it silently reverts to deterministic output.
findings.repro:
1. Build with VITE_PARTNER_BRIEFING_ENABLED=true on an Android 8.0+ device with the model AVAILABLE.
2. As the partner, post 6 text records in the same day and the same period (all 'morning'), each about 200 Latin characters — English, or Korean written in romanized/Latin form. Each is individually under 1000 graphemes, so none is force-fallbacked by chunk.ts.
3. As the viewer, open the partner's Story for that day.
4. All 6 items fit one batch by bytes (~1500 of the 2560 available), but totalGraphemes ~1200 > 1000, so Plugin.kt:261 returns null and the call is rejected E_BAD_REQUEST at Plugin.kt:108 before any inference runs.
5. The whole day's grouping falls back to deterministic; generation is reported as deterministic, never on_device.
findings.impact: For any day whose records are Latin-heavy, the on-device briefing silently never engages — every request is rejected before the model is even consulted, and the user sees only ungrouped deterministic output with no indication anything failed. It is the GATE 4 feature quietly not working, caused by the caller not honouring a limit the provider explicitly publishes in capability(). It also wastes a full bridge round trip and a batch's share of the 5s run budget per affected day.

In src/lib/partnerBriefing/pipeline.ts, add a total-grapheme test to canItemsFitInEnvelope (sum countGraphemes over every candidate of every item, reject when it exceeds envelope.maxInputTextGraphemes) so batchCandidateSegments at line 379 splits before the limit instead of after; chunk.ts already exports countGraphemes for this. No native change is needed — the Android side is the correct, stricter party.

  build.gradle:26   implementation 'com.google.mlkit:genai-prompt:1.0.0-beta2'

pulls com.google.mlkit:common:18.11.0, whose manifest declares minSdkVersion 21 and an <application> block. That block merges all the way into the shipped app manifest — android/app/build/intermediates/packaged_manifests/debug/processDebugManifestForPackage/AndroidManifest.xml:176-190:

    <provider
        android:name="com.google.mlkit.common.internal.MlKitInitProvider"
        android:authorities="app.gomsinlog.mlkitinitprovider"
        android:exported="false"
        android:initOrder="99" />

        <meta-data android:name="com.google.firebase.components:com.google.mlkit.common.internal.CommonComponentRegistrar" .../>

Android instantiates every declared <provider> during process creation, before Application.onCreate. MlKitInitProvider.onCreate initialises MlKitContext, which runs component discovery — a PackageManager.getServiceInfo(..., GET_META_DATA) binder call plus reflective instantiation of CommonComponentRegistrar. It is unconditional: it does not consult Build.VERSION.SDK_INT, and it does not consult VITE_PARTNER_BRIEFING_ENABLED, because it is manifest-level and the AAR is linked in either way. This is also load-bearing rather than removable — javap shows Generation.getClient() takes no Context, so it depends on MlKitContext being initialised by exactly this provider. The app manifest merger report at line 433 confirms the provider is ADDED from com.google.mlkit:common:18.11.0.

3. Before Application.onCreate runs, the process instantiates com.google.mlkit.common.internal.MlKitInitProvider and performs ML Kit component discovery. Observable as the provider in `adb shell dumpsys package app.gomsinlog | grep mlkitinitprovider`, and in the packaged manifest above.
